get.description:
Returns a paginated list of purchase debit notes for the account. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. It requires the **Inventory** plugin to be active.

A purchase debit note is a purchase document that shares storage with purchase orders and is identified by its document type. This endpoint returns only debit-note records.

### Data-level path segment

The trailing path segment (`-1`) is the **relation data level** — how deeply related records are eager-loaded — not a page number. Use `-1` (load base record with light relations only). Calling the list **without** a data level (`.../purchase_debit_note/list`) attempts to eager-load the full relation graph and fails with a `400` database error, so always include the segment.

### Pagination & query parameters

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>]` | Filter by a field's value, e.g. `filter[no]=PDN-0001` or `filter[supplier_id]=1`. |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `sort[date]=desc`. Default ordering is newest first (`id` descending). |
| `version` | Set to `2` to run each row through the listing formatter (adds display-formatted values); the top-level envelope is unchanged. |

**Filterable fields.** Filter with `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>` (the operator is optional; `filter[<field>]=<value>` uses a default match). The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `no` | string | `filter[no]=PDN-0001` |
| `supplier_id` | integer (supplier) | `filter[supplier_id]=1` |
| `date` | date | `filter[date][greater_than_equal]=2026-01-01` |
| `summary_total` | number | `filter[summary_total][greater_than_equal]=100` |
| `tags` | string | `filter[tags]=urgent` |

**Sortable fields.** Sort with `sort[<field>]=asc|desc`. The fields intended for sorting:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | date | `sort[date]=desc` |
| `no` | string | `sort[no]=asc` |
| `created` | datetime | `sort[created]=desc` |

The API will in fact filter and sort on any existing column of the record; the tables above list the fields the product surfaces for this entity. With no `sort`, results are ordered by `id` descending.

### Response

The response is a standard paginated envelope (`current_page`, `data`, `per_page`, `total`, `last_page`, and the page-URL/link fields). Each item in `data` is a flat purchase debit note record.

`payment_status` and `requisition_delivery_status` are returned as codes; their meanings are listed on those fields below.

parameters.description: Page number. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.description: Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `sort[date]=desc`. Fields intended for sorting: `date`, `no`, `created`. Default ordering is `id` descending.

post.description:
Creates a purchase debit note. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. It requires the **Inventory** plugin to be active.

A purchase debit note shares storage with purchase orders and is identified by its document type, so **`type` must be `14`** — sending a different type (or omitting it) fails with a `400` (`"error": "Record Not Found"`) because the entity can only be resolved for type `14`.

### Request body

The body is a flat JSON object. The account layer enforces exactly three required fields — omitting any of them returns `422`:

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `supplier_business_name` | Required, non-empty. |
| `draft` | Required. `1` = save as draft, `0` = finalized. |
| `summary_total.currency` | Required, non-empty (the currency of the totals object). |

In addition, `type` must be `14` for the record to save (enforced below the validation layer with a `400`).

All other fields are optional. `no` (the debit-note number) is generated automatically when omitted. `currency_code` and `supplier_id` are optional. Server-managed fields (`id`, `created`, `modified`, `branch_id`, `site_id`, `staff_id`, payment/summary totals) are assigned by the server.

### Line items

Line items are sent under the **`purchase_debit_notes_items`** array (each entry becomes a purchase-order-item row). Each item takes `product_id`, `item` (name), `description`, `unit_price`, `quantity`, `discount`, `discount_type`, `tax1`, `tax2`, and optional `col_3`..`col_5` extra columns.

### Statuses

`requisition_delivery_status`:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Received |
| 2 | Rejected |
| 3 | Pending |
| 4 | Partially Received |
| 5 | Partially Rejected |

On success the response is `{ "message": "...", "id": <new id> }`; the message is localized to the caller's language.

post.description:
Creates a new purchase order.

Send a `PurchaseOrder` object together with a `PurchaseOrderItem` array; optionally include a `Payment` object to record an immediate payment and a `PurchaseOrderCustomField` array. The only hard-required fields are `PurchaseOrder.supplier_id` and, for each line item, `item`, `quantity` and `unit_price`; most other fields are defaulted automatically (currency, date, number, store, branch).

The document `type` and `payment_status` are set server-side and any client values for them are ignored. Whether the order is saved as a draft is controlled by the `send` query parameter, not a body field.

On success the endpoint returns HTTP **202** with `{ "result": "successful", "code": 202, "id": <new id> }`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Response format suffix, e.g. `.json`.

parameters.name: send
parameters.description:
Optional save/send behaviour.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| draft | Save the purchase order as a draft (no number is assigned yet) |
| direct | Save and email it to the supplier |
| revised | Save and open the send-to-supplier flow |
| print | Save and prepare a printable copy |

Omit to save a normal (issued) purchase order.

Updates an existing purchase order.

Send the `PurchaseOrder` header object plus the full `PurchaseOrderItem` array (the supplied items replace the existing ones); optionally include `PurchaseOrderCustomField`. The `id` comes from the path. The only hard-required fields are `PurchaseOrder.supplier_id` and, per line item, `item`, `quantity` and `unit_price`. The document `type` is set server-side.

is_offline.description:
Whether the supplier is offline (no portal login).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Online supplier — `email` is required |
| 1 | Offline supplier — `email` is optional |

supplier_number.description: Visual identifier for the supplier. Assigned automatically when omitted.

staff_id.description: Staff member who owns the supplier. `0` means the account owner. For non-owner callers it is set automatically to the caller.

email.description: Supplier's email. Required unless the supplier is offline (`is_offline = 1`). Must be a valid, unique email.

password.description: Supplier portal password (write-only). Optional; minimum 4 characters.

confirm_password.description: Confirmation of `password` (write-only). Required to match `password` whenever a password is supplied.

active_secondary_address.description: 0/1 — whether the secondary address is active.

language_code.description: Default language code. Obtain valid values from the General Listing API using the `languageCodes` model.

default_currency_code.description: 3-letter currency code following the ISO 4217 standard.

attachment.description: Comma-separated list of attachment references. Must be a string — a JSON array is rejected.

last_login.description: Time of the supplier's last successful portal login.

suspend.description: 0/1 — whether the supplier account is suspended.

last_ip.description: Last IP address the supplier logged in from.

modified.description: Time the supplier was last updated.

follow_up_status.description: Follow-up status id. Obtain valid values from the Follow-up statuses listing with the `supplier` model.

bn1_label.description: Label for business number 1 (depends on country, e.g. Tax ID number).

bn2_label.description: Label for business number 2 (depends on country).

branch_id.description: Branch id. Obtain valid values from the General Listing API with the `Branch` model.

id.description: Identifier of the newly created supplier.

validation_errors.description: Present on validation failure. Maps the offending field to its error message(s). Also returned when `attachment` is sent as an array instead of a comma-separated string.
